children: Crude oil futures jumped ~4% on Thursday despite President Trump's social media statement that the U.S. is having "productive discussions" with Iran and
the country before next month's midterm elections.

Crude oil and refined product futures prices pulled back modestly from their highs of the day after Trump's post; they had moved sharply higher in morning trading following reports that Iran has increased attacks on oil tankers moving through the Strait of Hormuz and the approach of a hurricane threatening refiners along the U.S. Gulf Coast.
Even though Trump's comments would suggest that negotiations are progressing, the market may be starting to react less to the president's proclamations on Iran than earlier in the war.
"The market has heard it all before, and the pullback just isn't what it was in the past," Robert Yawger of Mizuho Securities said in a note.
The New York Times
reported later that the U.S. had drawn up plans for three days of strikes on Iranian drone and missile arsenals, energy facilities, and other sites.

The U.S. Treasury Department said it imposed fresh sanctions on Iran, targeting individuals, networks, and 17 vessels for transporting Iranian crude, oil products, and petrochemicals in an effort to increase economic pressure.

The number of vessels transiting the ‌Strait of Hormuz fell to the lowest since July 23 after attacks on tankers last week reached their highest since the start of the war, Reuters reported, citing Kpler shipping data.

"Crude crossing the strait fell 27% from a wartime high the week before, to ⁠at least 10.1M bbl/day... back to its September average, but 74% of its pre-war level," Kpler analysts Emmanuel Belostrino and Yui Torikata said in a note.

However, exports from the Gulf of Oman coast and the Red Sea improved to 6.7M bbl/day, more than twice pre-war levels, Kpler said, which helped keep overall exports of Middle East crude at pre-war levels.
Front-month Nymex crude
for November delivery jumped 3.6% to $91.49/bbl, its highest settlement value since October 1, and front-month Brent crude
for December delivery climbed 4.1% to $104.28/bbl, its best close since September 28.
Front-month Nymex RBOB gasoline (
) for November gained 2.5% to $3.3160/gal, and front-month Nymex November ULSD (
) surged 5.6% to $4.8829/gal, the best settlement values since October 1 and September 30, respectively.
U.S. natural gas futures

fell after the Energy Information Administration reported a higher-than-forecast 85 Bcf were added to natural gas stocks for the week ended October 2; the front-month contract shed 1.1% to $3.1680/MMBtu.

title: Oil finishes sharply higher even as Trump says no attacks on Iran before midterms
